A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPGym benchmark. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original RL experiments, including sample efficiency, generalization, puzzle-size comparisons, and appendix ablations and linear probes.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Puzzle generation, image sampling, actions, operational reward cases, and learning procedures are retained. The revised formal description does not establish an algorithm or implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet and DiffusionDB images, 3×3 and 4×4 puzzles, image and one-hot observations, and Easy/Hard OOD scenarios. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The PPO, SAC, and DreamerV3 comparisons retain the same pretraining, auxiliary-learning, augmentation, and decoder variants. Table 2 reorders SAC variants without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: Training budgets, preprocessing, stopping rules, success metrics, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Section 5.3's revised wording retains the existing 100-episode OOD evaluations.

E4.justification: The augmentation and temperature searches, decoder ablation, one-hot controls, linear probes, generalization tests, and continued-training analysis are retained. Revised mechanism explanations introduce no new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds and means with 1.96 standard errors. The correlation statistics and uncertainty practices are unchanged; scientific notation is reformatted.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and learning curves are unchanged, including the reordered Table 2. Section 5.1 newly observes that PPO performance deteriorates at similar rates with increasing pool size regardless of pretraining, adding a qualitative finding from the retained results.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds the observation map O: S×I→Ω and explicitly defines solvable states. It changes the reward signature from R: S×A→R to R: S→R, although Equation (1) still depends on action validity, introducing a formal inconsistency. Appendix learning objectives remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, three contributions, and central conclusions retain the same benchmark and representation-learning claims. The introduction foregrounds the out-of-the-box evaluation scope already stated in v4's Methods and Limitations.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 adds a hypothesis linking CURL's difficulties to insufficient shared image structure, alongside the retained appendix explanation about whole-image versus tile-level features. Sections 5.3–5.4 qualify memorization and probing interpretations and suggest regularization that discourages memorization. Most other mechanism explanations already existed in Appendix C.2.1.

D1.justification: Appendices A and B retain architecture listings, hyperparameters, augmentation instructions, hardware, runtimes, and implementation descriptions. Code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Bibliographic expansions concern existing references; the Manhattan-distance connection emphasized in Related Work was already explained in v4's reward discussion.

P1.justification: Extensive paragraph-level rewriting spans the Introduction, Related Work, benchmark description, results discussion, and Conclusion. Explanations and narrative emphasis change broadly, while the overall section and appendix sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adjusts arrows and adds a dashed agent timeline. Tables 1–2 refine captions, Table 2 reorders rows, and Tables 11 and 13 move earlier within the appendix. Figure 9 is repositioned; experimental plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: Section 3 improves conceptual clarity by distinguishing fixed image dimensions from a growing observation space and explicitly defining image-conditioned observations. Clearer qualifications in the results discussion also help readers assess the evidence. These are limited gains: empirical support is unchanged, and the new state-only reward signature conflicts with Equation (1)'s action-dependent cases.
